entities.summary:
Louis Comfort Tiffany was an American artist and designer who worked in the decorative arts and is best known for his work in art glass, especially stained glass and Favrile glass. He is associated with the art nouveau and aesthetic art movements. He was affiliated with a prestigious collaborative of designers known as the Associated Artists, which included Lockwood de Forest, Candace Wheeler, and Samuel Colman.

Tiffany designed stained glass windows and lamps, glass mosaics, blown glass such as vases, ceramics, jewelry, enamels, and metalwork. Louis Comfort Tiffany was a painters & sculptors from New York City (1848-02-18, New York City–1933-01-17). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Louis Comfort Tiffany's work in art glass and stained glass influenced the aesthetic of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, particularly in the United States. His designs were widely popularized through his company, which employed over 1,000 people at its peak.
